claims.text: NbMoTaW is a tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for use as an electrocatalyst.
NbMoTaW can provide enhanced HER and HOR catalytic activity compared with conventional catalysts.
NbMoTaW can provide enhanced electrocatalytic durability compared with conventional catalysts.
The proposed refractory high-entropy alloy is nanocrystalline.
The proposed alloy has a body-centered-cubic structure.
The alloy forms a uniform multielement solid solution.
The multielement composition induces local lattice distortions at the alloy surface.
The multielement composition tailors the surface d-band electronic structure.
Lattice distortion and d-band tailoring modulate the adsorption energies of hydrogen intermediates.
Synergistic effects among tungsten and the other refractory elements optimize the binding of HER and HOR intermediates.
The refractory high-entropy alloy provides an inherently robust matrix.
The alloy matrix is corrosion resistant under HER and HOR operating conditions.
Optimized intermediate binding lowers HER overpotentials.
Optimized intermediate binding accelerates hydrogen oxidation.
The robust, corrosion-resistant matrix maintains catalytic durability under harsh electrochemical conditions.
The NbMoTaW electrode should exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than standard Pt-based catalysts.
The NbMoTaW electrode should exhibit higher HER and HOR exchange current densities than standard Pt-based catalysts.
The NbMoTaW electrode should retain activity during long-term cycling better than standard Pt-based catalysts.
Performance improvements depend on the alloy's nanostructure and surface state and may be greatest at high current density or high temperature.
Direct experimental evidence for enhanced HER and HOR catalysis by refractory high-entropy alloys is currently limited.
